subject: ZenCommerce — POC playbook & next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@zencommerce.com>, Markus Feldman <mfeldman@zencommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-18T16:15:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today — quick recap & proposed kickoff

Hi Asha / Markus —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap while it's fresh and a suggested path to kick off a focused POC: 

Pain points you called out
- Recommender API 99th-pctl latency spikes causing visible UI jank during peak traffic (Black Friday profile concerns).
- High per-request cost from current hosted setup; want to understand tradeoffs between cost and latency.
- Need to ensure data residency controls for European customers (sensitive segments).

Primary goal for the POC
- Validate a production configuration that meets your product SLAs (99th < 150ms for recommendation endpoint under expected load) while reducing token cost per inference by at least 20% vs your baseline.

Proposed POC scope (2 weeks) — high level
- Ingest a sampled dataset (10k sessions) -> deploy a Redwood-hosted / dedicated inference config for recommender endpoint -> run prompt/eval sweep -> report on latency, NDCG@5 vs baseline, and unit cost.

Success metrics (initial)
- Performance: 99th percentile latency < 150ms at sample load (see baseline numbers in the attached playbook).
- Quality: NDCG@5 improvement or parity with your current model; track relevance delta per prompt set.
- Cost: token/unit cost target <$0.0015 per recommendation call (tunable via batching/quantization).

Owners / contacts
- Redwood: Vanessa Ortiz (AM) — vanessa@redwood.com (POC lead), Ben Carter (Solutions Eng) — ben@redwood.com (ops/config lead), Karthik Iyer — karthik@redwood.com (runtime/quantization lead)
- ZenCommerce: Asha Rao (Product) — asha@zencommerce.com (product lead), Markus Feldman (Infra) — mfeldman@zencommerce.com (infrastructure contact)

Immediate access checklist (what we need from ZenCommerce to start)
1) A short-lived IAM role or read-only AWS credentials scoped to the S3 sample bucket (or a signed URL for the dataset).
2) IP allowlist for Redwood egress if you plan to test against private VPC endpoints (we'll share IP ranges).
3) A small sample dataset (10k sessions) and an example request/response for the current recommender (so we can compute baseline).

Proposed kickoff: Tue Sep 23 at 10:00 AM PT. If that works for you we’ll send a calendar invite and the initial playbook.

Attachment: zencommerce-poc-playbook.pdf (pilot scope + baseline worksheet)

Thanks —
Vanessa
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

Subject: POC kickoff readout — scope, metrics, prompt suite, timeline, and access playbook

Hi Asha / Markus —

Thanks for the quick reply. Per your asks, attaching the lightweight POC playbook (zencommerce-poc-playbook.pdf) and the first-pass prompt suite (prompt-suite-v1.json). Below is an actionable kickoff readout you can forward to your infra/product teams.

Detailed scope (what Redwood will deliver)
- Endpoint: Recommend start with a single recommender endpoint (session-based personalization) to limit variables.
- Runtime configuration: start with 2 dedicated GPU workers (8k context if needed), continuous batching enabled, and KV caching for prefix reuse. We will iterate if load testing shows different needs.
- Eval: run the provided prompt-suite (examples below) against the sample dataset and compute NDCG@5, recall@10, and a precision/latency tradeoff table.

Prompt suite examples (from prompt-suite-v1.json)
- "Given session history X, recommend top 5 items ordered by purchase intent."
- "Suggest three complementary items for cart Y emphasizing margin uplift."
- "Rewrite headline to increase CTR while keeping product fidelity."

Success criteria (finalized during POC planning)
- Latency: 99th-pctl < 150ms under simulated expected QPS (we’ll run load tests).
- Quality: NDCG@5 delta >= +10% or parity for the most important segments.
- Cost: Achieve < $0.0015 per model call with batching/config tuning.

Timeline and milestones
- Sep 19-20: Access & dataset handoff (ZenCommerce) — provide IAM role and S3 path / sample CSV (10k sessions).
- Sep 21-22: Data ingestion + baseline run (Redwood) — compute baseline metrics and run initial prompt sweep.
- Sep 23: Joint kickoff & evaluation walkthrough (live) — review initial results, prioritize prompt/eval adjustments.
- Sep 24-26: Tuning and final report with recommendations (end of POC).

Owners (with primary emails)
- Redwood: Vanessa Ortiz — vanessa@redwood.com (POC coordination)
- Redwood SE: Ben Carter — ben@redwood.com (ops, infra config)
- Redwood Runtime: Karthik Iyer — karthik@redwood.com (quantization & perf)
- ZenCommerce: Asha Rao — asha@zencommerce.com (product)
- ZenCommerce: Markus Feldman — mfeldman@zencommerce.com (infra)

Access & security details
- Default retention: POC data retained for 30 days by default; we can configure deletion on project end or sooner on request — we'll include the retention clause in the playbook.
- SOC2: Redwood will provide SOC2 Type II attestations and a POC-specific security brief (attached link in drive).
- Networking: If you prefer private VPC routing, we’ll coordinate a whitelist; otherwise hosted sandbox will be used for the initial run.

Next steps checklist (what we need to start)
1) IAM role or transfer location for sample dataset (due Sep 20).
2) Confirmation on whether you need VPC/private egress (Markus to confirm).
3) Signoff on kickoff time (Sep 23, 10:00 AM PT).

Attachments referenced: zencommerce-poc-playbook.pdf, prompt-suite-v1.json

If you want, Ben and Karthik can join a short 30-minute run-through before kickoff to review the network and data schemas.

Thanks — looking forward to starting.

Vanessa Ortiz
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
